title.narrative: Integrated Health, SRH, GBV, and Disease Outbreak Response for Vulnerable Populations in Bama and Ngala LGAs during Lean Season.

description.narrative: ltpgtIn response to the heightened health concerns and access barriers facing women, girls, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups in Borno state during the lean season, this project seeks to enhance access to comprehensive integrated health care services, disease outbreak surveillance and response, malnutrition care, critical sexual and reproductive health (SRH) care, gender-based violence (GBV) prevention and response services in Bama and Ngala LGAs, through services in health facilities and by mobile health teams in IDP Camps/host communities.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtThe health component focuses on providing comprehensive integrated primary healthcare, preventive and curative services, including access to essential services, including immunization, treatment of minor illnesses, and MHPSS services. Also, it will strengthen early detection and rapid response to outbreaks, especially measles and malaria, as well as provide immediate treatment for SAM, critical SRH care including ANC, delivery, postnatal care, basic emergency obstetric and newborn care, Family Planning, and GBV prevention and response. Additionally, integrated management of childhood illnesses and prompt diagnosis and treatment protocols for cholera, acute watery diarrhoea (AWD), and typhoid fever will be enhanced. To mitigate and control potential disease outbreaks, the project will emphasize early warning systems, active case detection, and strategic prepositioning of essential diagnostic kits, pharmaceuticals, and supplies, complemented by the deployment of Rapid Response Teams (RRTs). Concurrently, culturally sensitive/appropriate risk and behavior communication and health education initiatives, incorporating community dialogues, will be implemented with the production of Risk Communication and Social behavioral change communication materials to enhance community awareness, promote gender equality, disability inclusion, and MHPSS.lt/pgtltpgt ltbrgtMobile medical teams, consisting of nurses, community health extension workers (CHEWs), and community health volunteers (CHVs), will extend outreach healthcare services to remote and hard-to-reach areas/ IDP camps, providing risk communication, disease surveillance, SRH services, hygiene promotion, and psychosocial support. Simultaneously, existing health facilities services will be strengthened through the provision of essential drugs, commodities, and trained personnel to ensure continuous care. Capacity building training for frontline health workers, including training in maternal and child care, SRH, and outbreak response, will further enhance the resilience of the health system. Additionally, the project will incorporate an integrated nutrition response, focusing on the early detection and treatment of malnutrition among children under five and pregnant and lactating women. This will include community-level screening, treatment of severe acute malnutrition (SAM) and moderate acute malnutrition (MAM) cases, and promotion of breastfeeding ltbrgtand appropriate complementary feeding practices, alongside strengthening linkages to stabilization centres for complicated cases.ltbrgtltbrgtThe GBV component will integrate awareness and prevention of gender-based violence and sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA) across all activities. Survivors will be connected to specialized referral services for medical, psychosocial, legal (if required), and protection support. Women and girls will be reached through safe space models, community sensitization, and dignity kit distribution, directly responding to NHF’s prioritized GBV activitiesltbrgtThis comprehensive integrated health and GBV project in Bama and Ngala LGAs is in sync with NHF’s 2025 Second Standard (Lean Season) Allocation Strategy and thus will mitigate the impacts of conflict, flooding, food insecurity, and underfunded health systems, thereby reducing morbidity, mortality, and protection risks for 32,200 affected, vulnerable at risk populations in targeted communities during the lean season.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
